strength.note: One engaged vessel in the Meteor–Bouvet duel. Nouveau Monde returned to port beforehand; Spanish Hernando Cortes was neutral. This does not imply equal crew sizes, tonnage or fighting power.

note:
The contemporary Hamburg report identifies the opposing North German gunboat Meteor and French aviso Bouvet. North German Confederation replaces the anachronistic German Empire identity for 1870. Meteor receives a small screw-gunboat analogy; Bouvet receives a three-masted screw-and-sail sloop analogy supported by the period museum model. These are equipment families, not exact hulls, rigs or gun arrangements. The Otago Witness account establishes one engaged vessel per side in the duel, excluding the departed French mail steamer and neutral Spanish escort. Ship counts do not imply equal crews, tonnage or fighting power. Contemporary accounts disagree on casualties; crew strengths and losses remain unknown. The catalogue date and coordinates are retained.

Equipment review: Meteor is represented by a small screw-gunboat family; Bouvet by a three-masted screw-and-sail sloop family. Meteor propulsion is explicit in the contemporary report; the period Bouvet museum model visibly has a stern propeller, funnel and sailing rig. Exact hulls, armament and national construction details are not reconstructed. This assignment requires the separately reviewed North German identity correction.
